stage1.impression: A clear ball on a black puck holds a floating Widmanstatten slice, but the slice is a near-white, low-contrast lattice of overlapping translucent bars that reads as frosted CG glass rather than etched iron. Hard clipped reflections (a white blob at the ball's foot, a stuck-on white square at upper left, a thick clipped right rim) pull the eye away from the meteorite.

blocking_9: The meteorite reads as etched grey iron: core lum_median 130-185 with lum_range > 90, not 228 with range 40
The Widmanstatten figure reads as a flat etched surface (fine dark taenite lines between grey kamacite bands), not stacked translucent 3D bars
No clipped hotspot larger than a glint on the ball: the foot blob at [770,800,1080,840] is 83% clipped
No softbox reflection reads as a pasted card over the slice ([640,340,720,450] median 234)
The ball's silhouette is drawn by a thin, graded rim, not a 20%-clipped band on the right
The ball stands off the cove: the cove is darker than the clear ball's interior (now both about 63-77)

changes.problem: The slice is washed to near white and flat, so the etch has no dark phase and the metal reads as frosted glass.

evidence.measured: lum_median 228.3, p5 200.6, p95 240.7, range 40; RGB 226/229/228, delta E2000 24 against a mid etched-iron grey #8A8C8E; vertical profile 191-233 across the slice

changes.expected: The camera-axis softbox no longer mirrors into the polished slice; the core drops to about 150-180 median and the kamacite bands separate from the darker taenite lines.

changes.problem: The polished, etched face mirrors a bright environment along the camera axis, so it has no dark phase. Etched iron needs a black field in its mirror direction to show the pattern.

evidence.measured: lum_p5 200.6: no pixel in the slice core goes below 200, so there are no dark lines at all

change.to: a matte black card 900 x 500 mm, reflectance 0.03, at (40, -1150, 244), facing the ball, sitting behind the camera and below the front light so it does not block the camera

changes.expected: The slice mirrors black between the bright kamacite facets; the core gains a dark tail (p5 below 90) while the bright bands stay above 190.

changes.problem: A hard clipped white ellipse at the ball's foot is the brightest thing in the frame and sits directly under the slice.
changes.expected: The refracted image of the overhead disc at the foot falls below clipping and grades into the warm LED line; the cap highlight stays readable (now median 207).

changes.problem: The key softbox's reflection is a hard white square on the ball's surface, over the slice's left edge, and it reads as a sticker.

evidence.measured: lum_median 234.4, p95 241, a flat field with straight edges

changes.expected: The key's reflection moves out to the ball's left limb, where it becomes a thin highlight, and the slice's left edge shows through clear acrylic (median below 140 here).

changes.problem: The right rim is a thick, clipped white band 58 px wide, so the ball reads as a thick-walled bowl, not a solid clear ball.

evidence.measured: clip_pct 20.08, p95 255; the right edge's 10-90 width is 58 px against 10 px on the left

changes.expected: The right rim becomes a graded highlight with only a sliver clipped, matching the left limb's weight.

changes.problem: The cove renders at the same mid grey as the ball's clear interior, so the clear acrylic has nothing dark to read against and the frame looks grey, not premium.

evidence.measured: cove lum_median 68.7 (lower corners 65-77) against the ball interior [800,660,1000,760] at 63.5

changes.expected: The cove falls to about 40-55 while the glow band behind the ball stays visible, so the ball's interior and rim separate from the ground.

changes.problem: The low front strip throws two bright fan streaks across the floor either side of the base, which read as stray spot leaks.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 114.7 against the floor beside it [300,1000,500,1060] p95 97; the left streak [540,1000,700,1060] p95 106

changes.expected: The floor streaks fade into the floor's tone, with p95 within about 8 levels of the plain floor.

out_of_scope.request: Replace the Widmanstatten figure: it is built from stacked, translucent, rectangular bars with visible depth and overlap, instead of a flat, etched, metallic face with fine taenite lamellae and plessite fields
out_of_scope.why: It is the biggest reason the hero fails to read as real meteorite. The card fixes what is inside the ball and offers no setting for the slice's material, so it needs the owner to change the slice's model or material (an opaque, metallic, anisotropic etched-iron surface).

out_of_scope.request: Show the slice's cut edge as a darker, rough rind
out_of_scope.why: The edge now reads as a thin, glassy green-grey outline. A dark rind is what tells the eye this is a slice of a real meteorite, but it is part of the fixed object.
